searches.reason: Develop intervention-based probes that distinguish reliance on sustained interests from reliance on isolated interactions or broad lexical similarity. Use chronological training prefixes, count- and position-matched perturbations, and residual-branch ablation to connect rank changes to specific components. Shuffled-text and popularity-matched controls should test whether apparent semantic dependence survives plausible shortcuts; these interventions measure model dependence, not causal user preferences.

searches.reason: Build an evidence-grounded failure taxonomy around the reported usefulness and compatibility failures. Seek methods that attach title or description spans to explicit specification conflicts, near-duplicate recommendations, and supported complements, while abstaining when evidence is insufficient. Validate annotation agreement and abstention quality on the twenty simulator users without inferring ownership, unmet needs, ratings, or latent traits.

searches.reason: Replace reliance on mean embedding cosine and sampler-dependent margins with a calibrated diagnostic panel: representation effective rank, score concentration, candidate-hardness sensitivity, and chronological training-prefix retrieval. Seek evidence that these probes predict distinct ranking failures across categories and controlled model changes. Keep auxiliary retrieval separate from pinned validation HR@10, use paired uncertainty where records exist, and account for repeated selection and the shared GPU budget.
